emails.subject: Harlow v. Kestrel Robotics — Case Strategy Conference — Apr 29 — AI Notetaker Summary
emails.body:
AI Notetaker — meeting summary
Meeting:  Harlow v. Kestrel Robotics — Case Strategy Conference — Apr 29
Host:     Nadia Bennett
Duration: 14:00 – 15:30 PT (90 min)
Attendees (full window): Nadia Bennett, Daniel Okafor, Rachel Moreno, Thomas Grant
Attendees (partial, left at 14:35 per scheduled expert segment): Dr. Helen Voss, Dr. Samuel Ortiz

— Expert findings —
• Dr. Helen Voss: actuator fatigue testing on six exemplar actuators from the same lot. None failed within four years at rated duty cycle. Cracking at the gear-housing boss appeared only at about 140% sustained load. The incident unit was not tested because it is still in the plaintiff's custody.
• Dr. Samuel Ortiz: controller logs came from Kestrel's service-portal backup. The load setpoint was raised on March 3 from a local Harlow terminal. Load stayed about 135–150% of rated until the March 21 failure. A firmware warning fired eleven times and was acknowledged and cleared locally. The terminal maps to a shared maintenance login rather than a named person.

— Logistics —
• Mediation set for May 12.
• SJ filing position due in two days; Rachel's cite check on the causation section wraps before then.
• Next expert deliverables: Voss's supplemental draft in about two weeks; Ortiz's timeline report and chain-of-custody declaration by May 8.

— Expert designation (deadline May 30) —
• Dr. Helen Voss: Working position is NOT to designate as a testifying expert. Daniel and Rachel aligned that her failure-mode opinion has a methodology gap. She tested six exemplars and never the incident unit, the cycle spread was wide, and she did not control for housing-casting batch. Opposing counsel could exploit this on cross-examination and in a Daubert challenge. Voss stays in a consulting role only.
• Dr. Samuel Ortiz: Designate as testifying expert. Controller-log methodology is clean, reproducible, and ties directly to the causation argument. Rachel to prepare the designation disclosure.

— Summary-judgment strategy & filing position —
• Lead argument: no genuine dispute on causation. Ortiz's timeline shows the March 3 setpoint change, eleven firmware warnings, and an adequate-warning alternative.
• Secondary argument: plaintiff's design-defect theory lacks a feasible alternative design. Harlow's expert report identifies none.
• Do not rely on Voss's fatigue data in the motion given the designation decision; cite exemplar testing only through Kestrel's internal QA records.
• Daniel drafts the causation section; Rachel finalizes the statement of undisputed facts; Nadia reviews tomorrow for filing prep.

— Witness strategy: Harlow engineer deposition —
• Primary goals: the shared maintenance login, and who raised the setpoint on March 3.
• Sequence: foundation and qualifications first, then the inspection timeline, then the logs. Hold the maintenance-record exhibits for the second half.
• Daniel takes the deposition; Rachel second-chairs. Dates still pending confirmation from opposing counsel.

— Draft declarations —
• QA lead declaration (v3): tighten paragraph 7 on lot-testing protocol, remove the speculative sentence on field conditions in paragraph 11, and conform the exhibit references to the statement of undisputed facts. Thomas to confirm the QA lead's title and tenure dates.
• Field technician declaration (v1): Rachel to do a first-pass edit; circulate to the case team via the DMS.

— Settlement authority —
• Client CEO Gerald Whitfield has authorized a settlement range ahead of the May 12 mediation; Thomas holds the specifics.

— Action items —
• Daniel Okafor — draft SJ causation section; confirm deposition dates with opposing counsel.
• Rachel Moreno — finish cite check; prepare Ortiz designation disclosure; first-pass edit on field technician declaration.
• Thomas Grant — confirm QA lead title and tenure dates; confirm the QA sampling language.
• Nadia Bennett — review SJ draft tomorrow for filing prep.

— End of summary —
